Implode the stencils of multiple pain drawings into one

Source: R/pdr_implode_stencils.R
pdr_implode_stencils.Rd

Collapses the .stencil elements of several pain drawings into a single stencil, by taking the union of the 1-regions of each .stencil. This is useful, for instance, for combining several anatomical region stencils into one larger region stencil.

Usage

pdr_implode_stencils(pdr_list, id = NULL)

Arguments

pdr_list

A pdr_list (see pdr_match()) where every pdr_drawing has a .stencil element (see pdr_add_stencil()). All drawings must have identical .width, .height and .units.

id

The .id of the resulting pdr_drawing. If NULL (default), "collapsed_<time>" is used.

Value

A pdr_list of length 1 with a single pdr_drawing whose .stencil is the union of the input stencils and whose .stencil_inverted is its complement. .points and .strokes are empty.

Details

The function is intended for use inside dplyr::summarise(), where the result should be a single drawing per group. All input drawings must have .stencil elements (see pdr_add_stencil()) and identical canvas dimensions and .units.

The result holds no strokes or points – it is a stencil, not a drawing. .file, .version and .app keep the common value if unique, otherwise "multiple" (or NA for .version). .timestamp is the maximum of the inputs (NA if all inputs are NA). The collapsed stencil is also stored in the alpha channel of .rgba (as a black image), so that pdr_plot_stencil() works on the result.

See also

pdr_add_stencil(), pdr_implode(), pdr_plot_stencil()

Examples

# \donttest{
pdr_stencil_full_body |>
  dplyr::summarise(pdr_data = pdr_implode_stencils(pdr_data))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 1
#>   pdr_data         
#>   <list>           
#> 1 <named list [13]>

pdr_stencil_full_body |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    view = ifelse(stringr::str_detect(id, "^Back_|^Mid_back"), "Back", "Front")
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    pdr_data = pdr_implode_stencils(pdr_data),
    .by = view
  )
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   view  pdr_data         
#>   <chr> <list>           
#> 1 Back  <named list [13]>
#> 2 Front <named list [13]>
# }
